cards.why: Ingrid sets Tomasz's hours and tasks from her father's care plan, supplies the tools and can end it: she controls what is done and how, so he is her household employee whatever his LLC or his request (Pub 926), and a household employee's wages go on a W-2, not a 1099-NEC. He is expected to be paid $4,512 in 2026, over the $3,000 threshold, so she should withhold his Social Security and Medicare from tonight's first pay; if she does not, she is responsible for his share as well as her own: 7.65% of $4,512, $345.17

Tomasz's first day of work for pay was Tuesday 6 October 2026; the employer signs Section 2 within 3 business days of it (8 CFR 274a.2(b)(1)(ii); USCIS), so by today, Friday 9 October. Ingrid examined his original US passport in person on 6 October and he signed Section 1 that day. A paperwork violation is fined at least $288 a form (8 CFR 274a.10(b)(2))

Marisol's W-2 profile holds a Social Security number ending 4471, typed in by hand, but her Social Security card on file reads ending 4417. Pub 926: keep the name and number exactly as on the card. A W-2 filed with the wrong number is an incorrect information return, $60 a return at the least tier the IRS publishes (for returns due in 2026), and Social Security could not credit her earnings

The third-quarter report is due by Friday 30 October 2026; filed now, the $75 late-report penalty is avoided. Covered wages paid in the quarter are Marisol's $8,418 alone: Felix's $2,592 is the employer's child's and not covered, Priya is Fernhollow's, Tomasz was first paid on 9 October, and Marisol's hours of 28 to 30 September were paid on 2 October, in the fourth quarter. She had $11,592 of covered wages before the quarter (Q1 $2,760, Q2 $8,832), so $4,408 of the $8,418 is under the $16,000 wage base; at 3.4%, the tax is $149.87

The third quarter's tax, $149.87 (3.4% of $4,408 of taxable wages), is due by Friday 30 October 2026; paid late it carries 10% of the unpaid tax, at least $25, and interest: $14.99 is under the minimum, so $25 is avoided

Tomasz is a new household employee whose wages are covered; Ostmere wants him reported within 20 days of his first day of work for pay, 6 October 2026, so by Monday 26 October. Filed now, the $25 late new-hire penalty is avoided
